newsitem.title: USA: AMR sees sales, tax pressuring Q3 yield.
newsitem.headline: AMR sees sales, tax pressuring Q3 yield.

text.p: American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, Wednesday said U.S. federal excise tax and fare sales would put pressure on its domestic operations in the third quarter, but the international outlook was strong.

"Domestically, because of some fare sales and low-cost carriers, and the return of the excise tax, we're going have some pressure on yield, but demand remains very strong," AMR Chief Financial Officer Gerald Arpey.
"Internationally, we're seeing demand up year-over-year, and we're seeing very good fare levels," Arpey said.

"I think on the domestic side, we're going to have a bit of a challenge, but the strength in the international operations will mitigate much of the potential domestic weakness," Arpey said in a conference call with reporters after the release of AMR's second-quarter earnings report.
Overall, advanced bookings exceeded last year's level, Arpey said.
Arpey also said he expected third-quarter unit costs to rise about three percent despite an expected 3.5 cents-per-gallon decline in fuel prices.
AMR ended the second quarter with about $2 billion in cash. Debt as percentage of total capitalization has fallen from about 84 percent in 1994 to about 65 percent in the second quarter, Arpey said.
